paper_title: TL;DR Too Long, Do Re-weighting for Effcient LLM Reasoning Compression
caption: Comparison of accuracy and generation length between Vanilla CoT and our method on four benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, AMC) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models. consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales.
model_annotation: The bar chart titled “DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B Generation Length Comparison” visually compares the average generation length in words for two methods — “Vanilla CoT” (light pink bars) and “TLDR (Ours)” (dark red bars) — across four mathematical reasoning benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical y-axis, labeled “Generation Length (words),” ranges from 0 to 8000 with major tick marks at intervals of 1000, and the horizontal x-axis lists the four datasets in that order. For GSM8K, the Vanilla CoT bar reaches 554 words, while TLDR reduces this to approximately 255 words, marked with a “-54%” label above the bar. For MATH500, Vanilla CoT generates 2861 words, and TLDR reduces it to about 1545 words, labeled “-46%.” On AIME, Vanilla CoT produces 6820 words, and TLDR reduces it to 6340 words, labeled “-7%.” For AMC, Vanilla CoT generates 4510 words, and TLDR reduces it to 3380 words, labeled “-25%.” The chart uses a legend in the top-right corner to distinguish the two methods by color, and percentage reductions are annotated above each TLDR bar to indicate the relative compression achieved. All bars are grouped by dataset, with Vanilla CoT always positioned to the left of TLDR within each group, and no sorting by value is applied across the x-axis. The chart visually emphasizes that TLDR consistently reduces generation length across all four benchmarks, with the most substantial reductions observed on GSM8K and MATH500.
